mathematics_checks: The four positive masses sum to one; each retained-coordinate fiber contains one 3/8 atom and one 1/8 atom, so its denominator is 1/2. For states s=(x,y), t=(u,v), the actual conditional kernels are P_X(s,t)=2*pi(t)*1[v=y] and P_Y(s,t)=2*pi(t)*1[u=x], whose rows sum to one.

Multiplying either factor by pi(s) gives 2*pi(s)*pi(t) times a symmetric retained-coordinate indicator, proving detailed balance. For either factor P, summing pi(s)*P(s,t)=pi(t)*P(t,s) over s gives (pi P)(t)=pi(t) by the row sum. With row-law convention the specified order is K=P_X P_Y, so pi K=(pi P_X)P_Y=pi; this does not imply K is reversible.

The first step leaves y fixed and the second step leaves the updated first coordinate u fixed. Only (u,y) can contribute to K((x,y),(u,v)), giving the product of the two stated conditionals, with the second conditional evaluated at u. The paths 00->00->01 and 01->01->00 give (3/4)*(1/4) and (1/4)*(3/4), respectively, both 3/16. Multiplication by the respective source masses 3/8 and 1/8 gives 9/128 and 3/128. These fluxes are the joint probabilities of the two ordered consecutive-state events under a stationary start; equality of unweighted probabilities does not suffice. The failed pairwise equality is compatible with the already proved equality of marginals.
